focus: Left post tib / arch + right shin

phase.name: Calm it down
phase.exit: Walking and daily life pain-free 3+ straight days, and the daily dose itself fully green.

note: Daily dose, ~12 min — after the session or in the evening with the Normatec. This is the LAST thing that gets dropped on a busy week.
pain_rules: Green: ≤3/10 working discomfort that settles within an hour — continue. Yellow: 4–5/10, or worse the next morning — back off a progression level. Red: sharp pain, limping, or pain at rest — stop that exercise and get the eval scheduled.
special: Left calf stays flat-ground, mid-range only — no end-range loaded calf work and no forced stretching until the ankle restriction releases. Right side can do the full menu.

exercises.name: Short-foot arch doming
exercises.cue: Squeeze and hold — pull the big-toe knuckle toward the heel, no toe curling. End the rep when the dome starts collapsing.

exercises.name: Isometric heel-raise hold
exercises.cue: Flat ground: rise halfway and hold — isometrics calm irritated tendons. Left stays mid-range; skip left if not green.

exercises.name: Banded ankle inversion
exercises.cue: Band around the forefoot, sweep the foot inward — slow and controlled; this is the post tib's own exercise. No band? Ankle over the opposite knee, press the inside of the forefoot into your palm.

exercises.name: Tibialis raises (wall lean)
exercises.cue: Heels on the ground, lift both forefeet — front-side work for the right shin.

exercises.name: Side plank + top-leg raise
exercises.cue: Hips stacked, lift the top leg while holding the plank — the standing progression of your clamshells.

exercises.name: Single-leg balance
exercises.cue: Barefoot, soft knee — post tib + hip coordination, not filler. Progress: eyes closed.

also: Massage gun / lacrosse ball on calves, soleus, and along the inner shin — 3–5 min/leg (muscle bellies, not the sore tendon or bone) until the deep-tissue massage is booked
Gentle left-ankle mobility only: circles + pain-free knee-to-wall rocks short of the stuck point — never push into the restriction
Evening Normatec + cold plunge — it measurably helped on 9/17
avoid: Loaded left calf work; forced left calf stretching
The plated Hyperion — even for walking around
